clue.text: Part of circuit training beginning with the morris dance?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word training is its first letter
the letters are set dancing, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fitness class whose routine opens with a spot of morris dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes T from 'training'; 'dance' rearranges T with THE MORRIS. 'circuit training' looks like gym talk, but the circuit is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperature-sensitive resistor is a component used in electrical circuits.

clue.text: Poet finding no rhyme for Jeremy Bentham, unfortunately

indicators.note: the name is unfortunately jumbled, and the poet's letters come out of it once some are set aside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: these letters are the ones left over

explanation.surface: A poet who cannot find anything to rhyme with the philosopher's name.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of JEREMY BENTHAM are the poet's name plus RHYME, signalled by 'no rhyme' and 'unfortunately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Betjeman was a twentieth-century English Poet Laureate.

clue.text: After the end of winter a tree appears more promising

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an osier is a willow tree

explanation.surface: Once winter is over, the trees look more hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes R from 'winter'; the osier follows it, as 'After' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rosier looks brighter or more hopeful, so its prospects are better.

clue.text: Pen must go on top of escritoire — there's a problem with the lid

parts.note: a pig pen is a sty

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pen must be placed on top of a writing desk, and its lid is faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes E from 'escritoire'. The lid is an eyelid, not the desk's lid.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid, so a trouble affecting that lid.

clue.text: Vehicle delayed initially in snowdrift is made late

indicators.note: the vehicle and letter are placed inside the drifting snow

parts.note: the word snow with its letters drifting gives SOWN
a truck is a vehicle

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word delayed

explanation.surface: A lorry held up in a snowdrift arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snowdrift' is read as snow drifting: the letters of SNOW rearranged. 'made late' means killed, not delayed: 'the late' is someone who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck down is to be killed, and 'the late' is an idiom for someone who has died.

clue.text: High spot for Jack entertained by Jacobin

indicators.note: the sailor is a guest held within the revolutionary

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a Jacobin of the French Revolution
jack and tar are both slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor finds a lofty spot while staying with a French revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain in Turkey where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest is a very high peak.

clue.text: Game crowd

definitions.meaning: a racket sport played in a walled court
as a verb, to cram or press tightly together

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a racket sport and also means to squeeze people tightly together.

clue.text: Company getting past, holding up victory in Europe

indicators.note: the word for past holds the turned victory letters inside it

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: VE as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A firm moving on while celebrating a European victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the VE (Victory in Europe) letters, as a down clue reads upwards; 'holding' then sets them inside the word for past.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group or company, especially of birds or people.

clue.text: A hot steam work-out that will stop bleeding

indicators.note: the letters are worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: A steam room session as a cure for a nosebleed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work-out' looks like gym talk but rearranges A HOT STEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A haemostat is a surgical clamp or agent that arrests the flow of blood.

clue.text: Hat or necklace or armband redhead removed

indicators.note: the letter is removed from the jewellery word

parts.note: a torque or torc is a metal neck ring or armband
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: Choosing between a hat, necklace or armband once a ginger-haired person has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes R ('redhead', the head of 'red') out of TORQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, as worn by chefs.

clue.text: Thatcher's injunction for Tim to embrace Sloppy Joe

indicators.note: the lyricist's surname surrounds the jumbled name

parts.note: Tim Rice, the lyricist

indicators.note: sloppy means the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister orders a lyricist to hug a careless man.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher told the press to 'Rejoice!' after the retaking of South Georgia in 1982; 'Sloppy' rearranges the name, which 'to embrace' sets inside the lyricist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher's famous command to celebrate was this single word.

clue.text: Not prepared for any rude letters

indicators.note: the letters of the words are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Unprepared for receiving obscene correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like post but says to rearrange ANY RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unready means unprepared, as in King Ethelred the Unready.

clue.text: Smyrna now is water, so to speak

indicators.note: the words are said out loud

parts.note: a mere is a lake, so water; 'is' stays as written

explanation.surface: Someone says the ancient city is now a body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'is mere' gives the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city of Smyrna is the modern Turkish port of this name.

clue.text: Token for hop-picker going to pot

indicators.note: going to pot means falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A voucher for a farm labourer who has let himself go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pot' rearranges HOP-PICKER; 'pot' also hints at the card game's kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaming counter used as a stake in cards is a kind of token.

clue.text: Rough pegs worked in potentially explosive situations

indicators.note: rough treatment knocks the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Crude pegs fashioned in situations that could blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' rearranges PEGS WORKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrels of gunpowder are a common figure for tense situations liable to erupt.

clue.text: Stiff examination

parts.note: reads as a hard test, but a stiff is slang for a corpse, so it is an inspection of a dead body

explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is a medical examination of a corpse to find the cause of death.

clue.text: Knotty Ash, perhaps, ends sound work by Hawthorne

parts.note: tangled and knotty both describe knots
ash is an example of a wood

indicators.note: the word for ends is heard spoken

parts.note: tails are the ends, as of coins or coats

explanation.surface: A Liverpool suburb gives a heard ending to a writer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Knotty Ash is a Liverpool district, made famous by the comedian Ken Dodd, which disguises the pieces. TAILS spoken gives TALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1853 book of Greek myths retold for children.

clue.text: Sweet ship? That's good?

definitions.meaning: a hard candy on a stick
the Good Ship of Shirley Temple's song

explanation.definitionFit: It is a sweet on a stick, and the Good Ship in Shirley Temple's famous song.

clue.text: Woody's line of fire

parts.note: igneous means of fire, as in volcanic rock

explanation.surface: A character called Woody describes a line of flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligneous is a technical adjective meaning made of or like wood.

clue.text: Chaps (two of them contractors) taking equal shares in plant

parts.note: three men's names, each three letters: Roy
Alf, short for Alfred
Ern, short for Ernest

explanation.surface: Three men, two of them builders, splitting a factory equally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'equal shares' means three names of three letters each; 'contractors' means shortened names (ALF and ERN), not builders.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fern, Osmunda regalis, is a plant.

clue.text: Chicken or canary, perhaps

definitions.meaning: canary is an example of a shade of this colour

explanation.definitionFit: The word means cowardly, and it is the colour of which canary is a shade.

clue.text: Be a fool about a lady of rank

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about here means turned round

parts.note: a mug is a fool

explanation.surface: Advice to act the idiot around a noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for a fool; 'Be a fool' reads as one instruction, but BE stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A begum is a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia.

clue.text: They may be beaten in spring (before start of summer)

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the word summer

explanation.surface: Something that gets thrashed in spring, ahead of summer arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: Beating the bounds is an old English parish custom of walking the boundary and striking it with sticks. 'spring' is a season in the surface but a leap here.
explanation.definitionFit: Parish boundaries are traditionally beaten in the ceremony called beating the bounds.

clue.text: Crusoe's original place in Scotland

definitions.meaning: Alexander ..., the castaway who inspired Robinson Crusoe
a town in the Scottish Borders

explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Selkirk was the real castaway behind Defoe's novel, and the name is also a Borders town.

clue.text: A drink for Pete's follower

definitions.meaning: the word that follows 'for Pete's' in the exclamation

explanation.definitionFit: It is a Japanese rice wine, and the word completing the exasperated exclamation 'for Pete's ...'.

clue.text: Arrogance demonstrated in flashback by film director

parts.note: the back of the word flash is its last letter
an auteur is a film director with a distinctive personal style

explanation.surface: A director's conceit shows in a scene set in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashback' is read as 'flash back', the back letter of 'flash', not a scene from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughty pride, a disdainful manner of superiority.

clue.text: Kid giving old Vietnamese leader a kiss

parts.note: Ho Chi Minh led North Vietnam
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A kid gives the former Vietnamese leader a peck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is a verb here, meaning to fool, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid is to fool someone, and a hoax is a trick played on them.

clue.text: Capital before Tokyo rose — or Tokyo collapsed?

indicators.note: the second city name collapses and its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a city came before Tokyo grew, or Tokyo fell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tokyo rose' may recall the wartime broadcaster, but here it means Tokyo rose to prominence.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto was Japan's imperial capital for over a thousand years until 1868, when Tokyo took over.

clue.text: Member of ruling class in naked drug orgy!

indicators.note: an orgy is a wild scene, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An aristocrat caught up in a naked drug-fuelled party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orgy' rearranges NAKED DRUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand duke is a sovereign or high-ranking prince, so a member of a ruling family.
